questions.q: This lesson defines lateral movement as:
options: A single, highly sophisticated technique unique to advanced attackers
Using access or credentials gained from one compromised host to reach additional hosts in the same environment
A type of malware that spreads without any credential involved
A network scanning technique used only in the reconnaissance phase
questions.explain: Lateral movement is fundamentally about reusing a valid credential or trust relationship somewhere else it's also valid, not a single dramatic exploit.

questions.q: Why is lateral movement generally detectable?
options: It never actually generates any log data
SIEMs only detect lateral movement if an attacker announces it
Legitimate authentication infrastructure already records authentication events, which a SIEM can correlate against expected patterns
It can only be detected after the engagement report is written
questions.explain: Windows event logs, SIEM correlation, and EDR telemetry already log authentication events, which is exactly the data a detection rule correlates against baseline behavior.

questions.q: A domain admin account logging into a line-of-business laptop, rather than only management infrastructure, is an example of:
options: A baseline deviation that a SIEM watchlist or analytics rule can be built around
Normal expected behavior that never needs investigation
A finding that has nothing to do with lateral movement
A pattern that only matters if it happens more than once
questions.explain: A privileged account appearing somewhere it's never used breaks an expected usage pattern — exactly the kind of deviation detection content is built to flag.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is nearly every lateral-movement detection signature ultimately a symptom of?
options: A firewall rule that was misconfigured during initial setup
An identical, reusable credential crossing a boundary it shouldn't have
A software bug unrelated to identity or credentials
An outdated antivirus signature database
questions.explain: The lesson frames credential reuse across a boundary as the root cause behind nearly every detection signature discussed — which is why credential hygiene is as important as detection.

questions.q: What course 8 content does this lesson say matters as much as detection for defending against lateral movement?
options: Cost optimization and FinOps tagging strategy
Container image vulnerability scanning
Terraform module versioning practices
Unique local administrator passwords, credential tiering, and Privileged Access Workstations
questions.explain: Course 8's identity engineering content on credential tiering and PAWs, combined with this course's microsegmentation content, removes the reusable credential that most lateral-movement signatures depend on.
